name: Farlis
city: Terfila, Görff, Khol Moshin, Feria del Milenio
backstory: Member of the Collective. Travels the Khol Moshin-Görff route on horseback. Originally from Terfila, a relative of the town's aristocratic family, which has had a stable financial situation for centuries. Moved to Görff years ago to join the revitalization of the abandoned citadel — he likes the romanticism (and the humor) of turning what was once a tyrant's castle, way back in time, into the opposite of that, though beyond the joke he genuinely believes it just makes more sense to share things; not that deep, plain common sense. Has been waiting years for the Feria del Milenio, ever since first hearing about it from the Peregrins, and is having a field day going pavilion to pavilion like a kid in a candy shop now that the thousand-year mark has finally arrived. Likes magnificent tales.

experience: Waiting with Khaoe at the Feria del Milenio, by the Castillo de Görff replica in the Plaza de las Culturas, for Khaasan, expecting him to arrive by griffon.
Picked up from Khaoe in this conversation: that every temple in Lundria kept its own calendar, as if the world began again at each door.

Finds it poetic justice that he and Khaoe now live in the same castle that once belonged to a tyrant, long before the Collective — Khaoe doesn't share the romantic framing, sees it as plain necessity instead.
Ran into Aureobalo at a bar in Salthos Cruzados, the first evening of the Feria del Milenio — already knew him from before (their routes cross), but a first for meeting at this particular place.
Confirmed to Aureobalo, when he brought back a vaguer version of it secondhand, that the castle/poetic-justice remark really was his own, and that Khaoe was the one who shot it down.
Same evening, same bar: Khaoe noticed he'd been talking with Aureobalo; asked her in turn about her trip to Lundria, and got back that she came home with more questions than she left with.
Learned from Bardaglis, same evening, that the castle line has already become a song lyric — though the part that stuck was Khaoe's rebuttal, not his own poetic-justice framing.
Names the Castillo de Gorff replica in the Plaza de las Culturas as his favourite thing in the whole Feria - you cannot see the shape of a castle from inside it.
Conceded to Aureobalo that Khaoe was right in the part that matters: poetic or not, the castle was one man's and no longer is, and his joke about it changes nothing. Keeps the joke, drops the claim.
Says he arrived at the Collective with a Terfila surname and left it in Terfila - it is useful for nothing there, which is exactly what it is for.
Picked up from Aureobalo: that his surname resembles the losing side of the Guerras de Gorff, that he is unrelated to them, and that his parents' admiration for the loyalists was never his choice.
Found Gok at the Espiral de las Eras alcove, a man keeping the Hotel Kholi's story alive at the Feria del Milenio, who understands that monuments are the keeper's work, not the stone.
Recognized in Gok's devotion to the Hotel Kholi the same principle he lives by with the Castillo de Görff — that what we leave behind, and how we hold it, is what makes it matter.
Visited the Alcoba of the Guerras de Görff in the Espiral de las Eras and met Auroboro III, an old descendant of officers from those wars.
Auroboro III clings to the Guerras as glorious heritage and ancestral honor; sees forgetting as spiritual death.
Auroboro III called Farlis a fool for rejecting the past, but Farlis holds that he builds real things rather than talking about ghosts.

criterion.standard: counts a life well spent if what he leaves behind is a place that used to be one man's and isn't anymore
criterion.wasted_life: inheriting a name and a house and handing both on unchanged
criterion.trusts: a magnificent tale, and whoever is willing to put their name to it
criterion.distrusts: a plain accounting that leaves out why the thing mattered
cost_ledger: Khaoe rejected his poetic-justice framing of the castle to his face - to her it was plain necessity, someone had to take up the stones (khaoe_farlis_el_castillo_que_fue).
Learned from Bardaglis that the line which survived into song was Khaoe's rebuttal, not his own framing (farlis_bardaglis_bar_salthos_cruzados).
Gave up the poetic-justice framing itself in front of Aureobalo - the third time the reading has been contested and the first time he let it go (aureobalo_farlis_castillo_en_miniatura).

history.cause: khaoe_farlis_el_castillo_que_fue#3, retold to him by Aureobalo
history.note: Gate matched: the claim references the castle at Gorff, the case his anchor (doran_four_castles#6) is read off. He could not dismiss it - it came from Khaoe, named and firsthand, which is exactly the kind of source he trusts, and he had already heard it from her directly. Susceptibility was high: two prior cost_ledger entries on this same reading. Outcome is reinterpretation rather than a break, because the anchor fact (the castle's scarred past) is untouched - what he gave up was the ornament, not the standard. Standard unchanged, tempered 0 -> 1.
history.trust_note: trusts/distrusts deliberately left untouched. Step 6's rule that surviving a refutation hardens distrust against that kind of source only makes sense for the *reject* move; hardening him against named firsthand testimony after he accepted it would be backwards. See TODO.
